# #1554: Patch: ladder bots draw realistic usernames (edgy, nonsense, real-world refs)
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

A ladder bot's username (R1454) today is either `Player#n` (30%, `BOT_DEFAULT_USERNAME_SHARE`) or one word from each of two tidy lists, `BOT_NAME_FIRST` × `BOT_NAME_SECOND` in `crates/server/src/config.rs` (`QuietOtter`, `JollyMuffin`, `CosmicPickle`). That's 576 names, all in one CamelCase-adjective-animal shape, which reads like a children's-app name generator. Nobody on a real ladder names themselves that way. People pick names with more edge (`VoidReaper`, `xXdoomXx`, `DeezNuts`), more nonsense (`blorpington`, `skrunkly`), real-world references (anime, memes, politics: `Itachi_Uchiha`, `GojoMain`, `Obamna`, `BernieBro`), Chinese names in characters and pinyin (`小龙`, `咸鱼666`, `xiaoming99`, `WangLei`), lowercase run-ons, numbers and birth years (`kev2009`, `nightfall_77`), underscores, doubled letters and leetspeak. And there's always a Luis: `Luis`, `luis2007`, `LuisitoGamer`, `xX_Luis_Xx`, `Luis#4`. This patch replaces the two lists with a username grammar that produces that mix, so a bot's name doesn't give it away. Some of the names should make a reader go "damn, that's a bit much": that's what a real ladder looks like.

**The constraints a name must pass** (unchanged, `crates/server/src/username/`, R1432–R1434): 2–16 user-perceived characters; letters, decimal digits and `_` only (no `.`, `-` or spaces, so `xX_name_Xx` works but `x.name.x` doesn't); one script (so a Han name never mixes in Latin letters: `小龙666` is fine, `小龙Gamer` is refused); the blocklists (`blocklist_token.txt`, `blocklist_anywhere.txt`). A taken base gets the lowest free `#n` tag, which is fine because real players get tags too (and is exactly how a ladder full of Luises looks).

**On a corpus of real usernames:** the public corpora of common usernames are almost all scraped or leaked account lists (credential dumps, the "top usernames" files in security wordlists, which are mostly `admin`/`root`/`user` anyway). We shouldn't sample from them. Those handles belong to real people, a bot would end up wearing someone's real handle from another site, and the licensing and provenance aren't clean. Use these instead:

1. **A shape grammar.** A weighted list of templates, each a named constant with its share, for example:
   - `{word}{word}` in CamelCase, lowercase or with `_` between the words
   - `{word}{digits}`: a 2-digit number, a birth year `19xx`/`20xx` from a plausible range, or `69`/`420`/`1337`-style filler
   - `xX{word}Xx` / `xX_{word}_Xx`
   - `The{word}`, `{word}{word}TV`, `{word}YT`, `{word}Gaming`, `El{word}` (`ElLuis`, `ElCrack`)
   - reference shapes: `{ref}Main`, `{ref}Fan`, `{ref}Stan`, `Not{ref}`, `{ref}Kun`, `{ref}_{digits}`, `{ref}4Life`, `{ref}Enjoyer`, and a reference's own two-word form (`Itachi_Uchiha`, `GojoSatoru`)
   - whole memes that are names on their own (`DeezNuts`, `Ligma`, `SkillIssue`, `TouchGrass`, `Obamna`), used bare or with a suffix
   - given-name shapes: `{name}`, `{name}{digits}`, `{name}_{initial}`, `{name}{initial}`, `{name}ito`/`{name}ita` diminutives, `{name}Gamer{year}`
   - Chinese shapes (see the register below): a Han name bare or with digits; pinyin surname + given name (`WangLei`, `zhang_wei`, `liuyang`), with or without digits
   - leetspeak on one word (`a→4`, `e→3`, `o→0`, `i→1`), applied to part of the draws only, never to Han or to given names
   - stretched letters (`brooooo`), a doubled final letter (`ghostt`), `ii`/`zz`/`_` suffixes
   - pure nonsense: syllables strung from a small consonant-vowel table (`blorp`, `zindle`, `quorbo`), or a short keyboard mash (`asdfjkl`, `qwop`)
2. **Word lists by register**, kept as data files beside the pool (`crates/server/src/bots/names/<register>.txt`, read with `include_str!`), not config arrays. Each list should be big enough (roughly 60–150 entries) that repeats are rare. Registers:
   - **edgy:** `Reaper`, `Void`, `Doom`, `Toxic`, `Sniper`, `Rogue`, `Venom`, `Hex`, `NoScope`, `Slayer`, `Demon`, `Carnage`
   - **crude and meme bait:** `DeezNuts`, `Ligma`, `Sugondese`, `Ben_Dover`, `ur_mom`, `BigChungus`, `GigaChad`, `SigmaGrindset`, `SkillIssue`, `Copium`, `TouchGrass`, `L_Bozo`, `Ratio`, `Skibidi`, `OhioFinalBoss`, `TaxEvader`, `GenevaSuggestion`, `NoMercy69`
   - **anime:** characters (`Goku`, `Vegeta`, `Naruto`, `Sasuke`, `Itachi`, `Kakashi`, `Luffy`, `Zoro`, `Gojo`, `Sukuna`, `Levi`, `Eren`, `Mikasa`, `Denji`, `Makima`, `Ryuk`, `Light_Yagami`) and the vocabulary (`Senpai`, `Baka`, `Kawaii`, `Waifu`, `Weeb`, `Otaku`, `UwU`, `Nya`, `Sama`, `Chan`)
   - **Chinese**, two files:
     - *Han* (`chinese_han.txt`, 2–4 characters each): nickname forms (`小明`, `小龙`, `阿伟`, `阿杰`, `老王`, `大白`), gamer slang (`菜鸟`, `大佬`, `大神`, `无敌`, `战神`, `咸鱼`, `摸鱼`, `佛系玩家`, `夜猫子`), optionally followed by digits from the Chinese-internet set (`520`, `1314`, `666`, `999`, `8`) or a birth year
     - *pinyin* (`chinese_pinyin.txt`): common surnames (`Wang`, `Li`, `Zhang`, `Liu`, `Chen`, `Yang`, `Huang`, `Zhao`, `Wu`, `Zhou`) and given names (`Wei`, `Lei`, `Yang`, `Jie`, `Hao`, `Xiaoming`, `Jun`, `Ming`, `Yu`), plus pinyin slang (`laowang`, `dalao`, `xiaobai`, `ahwei`), drawn as `WangLei`, `zhang_wei`, `liuyang666`, `laowang520`
     - `88` (bye-bye in Chinese) is left out: it collides with the extremist code `never.txt` bans.
   - **given names**, weighted, with a skew toward Spanish-speaking names: `Luis`, `Jose`, `José`, `Juan`, `Carlos`, `Miguel`, `Alejandro`, `Diego`, `Jorge`, `Andres`, `Sofia`, `Valentina`, `Camila`, plus `kev`, `jess`, `tommy`, `mike`, `alex`, `chris`, `sam`. **Luis is the single most common name on the ladder:** `BOT_NAME_LUIS_SHARE` (start at 2% of all bots, so a full pool of 200 has about four Luises, the later ones tagged `Luis#1`, `Luis#2` …), across the given-name shapes (`Luis`, `luis2007`, `Luis_M`, `LuisG`, `Luisito`, `LuisitoGamer`, `ElLuis`, `LuisFer`, `xX_Luis_Xx`)
   - **politics and public life:** meme and nickname references, spread evenly across the spectrum so no side dominates: `Obamna`, `DarkBrandon`, `LetsGoBrandon`, `BernieBro`, `FeelTheBern`, `Trump2028`, `MAGAmain`, `AOC_Stan`, `RonPaulFan`, `TaxationIsTheft`, `CommunismEnjoyer`, `Libertarian69`, `Kamala_Coconut`, `Thatcher_Stan`
   - **other real-world refs:** game and pop-culture characters and memes (`Shrek_Is_Love`, `Thanos_Did_Nothing_Wrong` trimmed to fit, `MasterChief`, `Kratos`, `JohnWick`, `Creeper`, `AmongUs_Sus`); characters and memes only, never a real streamer's or creator's handle
   - **plain nouns and animals** (keep most of today's lists), **nonsense words**, **food and objects**, and **gamer filler** (`Pro`, `Noob`, `Tryhard`, `Main`, `GG`, `Crack`)
3. **Optional, by a person, not the bot:** if the server's own players' names are a useful sample, measure the *shares of shapes and registers* among them (how many are lowercase, have digits, have `_`, reference anime, are in Han, and so on), never the names themselves, and set the weights from that.

**How far the edge goes.** These names are written by the studio and worn by the studio's own accounts, and the shared filter is light on purpose (R1433: 64 words, made for people's names, not for curating a list). So "the filter let it through" isn't enough. The line:
- **In:** crude, juvenile and innuendo humor (`DeezNuts`, `Ligma`, `Ben_Dover`), mock violence and gamer trash talk (`NoMercy`, `L_Bozo`, `Carnage`), dark-ish meme jokes (`GenevaSuggestion`, `TaxEvader`), partisan political references and memes (`LetsGoBrandon`, `FeelTheBern`), `69`/`420`.
- **Out, even when the filter passes it:** slurs and their soundalikes, in any language the lists use (English, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese romanised); hate or extremist references and codes (`1488`, `88`, `HH`, `SiegHeil`, `Groyper`, terror groups); explicit sexual terms; names that read aloud as a blocklisted word (`Hugh_Jass`, `Mike_Hunt`); self-harm; real tragedies and their victims; and any real person combined with a violent, sexual or crude word.
- **Real people:** a public figure appears only as a reference (a meme spelling, nickname or slogan: `Obamna`, `DarkBrandon`, `BernieBro`, `Trump2028`), never as a bare full name and never as a `Real…`/`Official…`/`The_Real…` handle, so no bot poses as the person.
- **How it's enforced, at draw time:** a bot-only exclusion list, `crates/server/src/bots/names/never.txt` (whole tokens and substrings, the same folding as R1433's, Han entries matched as substrings), checked against every drawn name, on top of the shared blocklists; a hit is redrawn. And the grammar never combines the politics and public-life register with the edgy or crude registers, and never emits a `Real`/`Official`/`The_Real` prefix.

**Rules of the draw**
- Still drawn from the pool's seed (`draw_new_bot`, `Rng`), so the same seed makes the same bot.
- `BOT_DEFAULT_USERNAME_SHARE` stays: some people really do keep `Player#n`.
- Each register has a named share (`BOT_NAME_SHARE_*`) so the edge stays a seasoning rather than the whole ladder. Start around: plain/nonsense/gamer 35%, edgy 12%, anime 13%, Chinese 10% (Han and pinyin about half each), given names 9% (Luis's 2% inside it), crude/meme 9%, other refs 6%, politics 6%. The builder may tune these, but must keep each named, and Luis must stay the most common given name.
- A drawn name that `normalize_username`, the shared blocklists or `never.txt` refuses is drawn again, up to a named `BOT_NAME_DRAW_ATTEMPTS`, before the bot falls back to `Player#n`. Today a refusal goes straight to `Player#n`, which would quietly push the default share up once edgier words make refusals more common. (R1433 reads digits among Latin letters back as letters, so some `laowang520`-style draws may be refused; the redraw covers it.)
- Only new bots get the new names. Bots already in the pool keep theirs: renaming a whole ladder at once would look stranger than the names do, and the pool keeps meeting the same faces (R1454).
- Every number (shares, digit ranges, year range, stretch length, attempts) is a named constant in `crates/server/src/config.rs` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

**No new tests (the owner's call).** The names are flavour. Don't add tests for the grammar, the shares, the lists or the edge line. Update existing tests only where this change breaks them (for example any that name `BOT_NAME_FIRST`/`BOT_NAME_SECOND`). So that `cargo jackioh spec check` needs no new proving test, **don't add a new ruling note**: rewrite R1454's username bullet in place (`spec/rulings/R1454.md`, and §9.12 if it repeats the old lists) to describe the grammar, the registers and the edge line.

Touches: `crates/server/src/bots/pool.rs` (`draw_new_bot`), `crates/server/src/config.rs` (remove `BOT_NAME_FIRST`/`BOT_NAME_SECOND`, add the grammar's constants), the new word-list files and `never.txt`, and R1454's username bullet. Server only: no engine, client or wire change. The shared player filter (`crates/server/src/username/blocklist_*.txt`) is not changed by this patch.

### Acceptance

- `draw_new_bot` draws names from the grammar and registers above; `BOT_NAME_FIRST`/`BOT_NAME_SECOND` are gone.
- A drawn name that `normalize_username`, the shared blocklists or `never.txt` refuses is redrawn, up to `BOT_NAME_DRAW_ATTEMPTS`, then falls back to `Player#n`.
- Existing bots keep their names.
- R1454's username bullet describes the new grammar and the edge line; `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p jackioh-server` are green (existing tests, updated only where they break).

None. Related: R1454, R1432, R1433 (#638 / #636).

/// R1433's matching against a caller's own lists: each `anywhere` entry wherever it appears in the
/// folded name, each `token` entry as a whole token (digits read back both ways, a token without a
/// letter never matched), every entry folded as the name is. The ladder bots' `never.txt` (R1454).
pub(crate) fn matches_lists(name: &str, anywhere: &[&str], token: &[&str]) -> bool {
    let folded = fold(name);
    if anywhere.iter().any(|word| folded.contains(fold(word).as_str())) {
        return true;
    }
    [ReadBack::All, ReadBack::Inner]
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|digits| tokens(&read_back_digits(name, digits)))
        .filter(|part| part.chars().any(is_letter))
        .map(|part| fold(&part))
        .any(|part| token.iter().any(|word| part == fold(word)))
}

/// R1433's matching against a caller's own lists: each `anywhere` entry wherever it appears in the
/// folded name, each `token` entry as a whole token (digits read back both ways, a token without a
/// letter never matched), every entry folded as the name is. The ladder bots' `never.txt` (R1454).
pub(crate) fn matches_lists(name: &str, anywhere: &[&str], token: &[&str]) -> bool {
    let folded = fold(name);
    if anywhere.iter().any(|word| folded.contains(fold(word).as_str())) {
        return true;
    }
    [ReadBack::All, ReadBack::Inner]
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|digits| tokens(&read_back_digits(name, digits)))
        .filter(|part| part.chars().any(is_letter))
        .map(|part| fold(&part))
        .any(|part| token.iter().any(|word| part == fold(word)))
}
```

pub fn draw_username(rng: &mut Rng) -> Option<String> {
